Measurement Invariance Across Groups

Source: R/measurement_invariance.R
measurement_invariance.Rd

Fits the standard ladder of multiple group invariance models for a measurement model of any number of factors and reports the comparison of its rungs in one table: configural invariance (same pattern, all parameters free by group), metric (equal loadings; required before comparing relations involving the factor), scalar (equal loadings and intercepts; required before comparing factor means), and strict (equal residual variances as well; required before comparing observed-score variances). With ordered indicators a thresholds rung comes first, because thresholds rather than intercepts carry the location information (Wu & Estabrook, 2016); with dichotomous indicators the two are not separately identified, so that rung is folded into metric. Each rung is tested against the previous with a likelihood ratio test, scaled when the estimator in force carries a robust test, which is what declaring ordered items arranges, and the practical-fit changes (delta CFI, delta RMSEA) are reported alongside, since with large samples the chi square will flag trivial differences (Cheung & Rensvold, 2002, suggest delta CFI of about -.01 as a red flag). The fitted lavaan objects come back as an attribute, so score tests and partial invariance refits do not require refitting the ladder. Requires lavaan.

Usage

measurement_invariance(
  data,
  model = NULL,
  group,
  items = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  ordered = NULL,
  estimator = "ML",
  missing = "fiml",
  group_partial = NULL,
  parameterization = c("delta", "theta"),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame with the items and the grouping variable.

model

The measurement model, given either as lavaan model syntax (a single string, or a character vector of lines that is collapsed with newlines, such as c("visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3", "verbal =~ x4 + x5 + x6")) or as a named list mapping each factor name to a character vector of its item names, from which the syntax is built. Exactly one of model and items must be supplied. An indicator of either form that data lacks is refused with an error of class dmar_items_invalid (see dmar_metadata).

group

Single character string naming the grouping column (two or more groups).

items

Character vector (three or more) naming the indicator columns of a single factor. A convenience for the one-factor (congeneric) case of cfa_1, equivalent to model = "f =~ item_1 + item_2 + ...". Exactly one of model and items must be supplied. Items that cannot be read from data (a name that is not a column, a name given twice, fewer than three) are refused with an error of class dmar_items_invalid.

levels

Which rungs of the ladder to fit, in order: any leading subset of the ladder in force. With continuous indicators the ladder is c("configural", "metric", "scalar", "strict"); with ordered indicators it is c("configural", "thresholds", "metric", "scalar", "strict"); when every indicator is ordered and dichotomous it is c("configural", "metric", "scalar"), because neither the thresholds nor the strict rung is identified for a two-category item (see ordered below). NULL (the default) fits the whole ladder in force.

ordered

Ordered categorical (including binary) items: TRUE for every indicator in the model, or a character vector naming the ordered ones. NULL (default) treats all indicators as continuous. Declaring ordered items switches the ladder and, unless the estimator already carries the mean and variance adjusted test, switches the estimator (see estimator below). The number of observed categories per declared item is counted before the ladder is built, because a dichotomous item has a single threshold that is not separately identified from the intercept of its underlying response (Millsap & Yun-Tein, 2004; Wu & Estabrook, 2016), and its residual variance is not a free parameter under either parameterization. When every declared item is dichotomous the thresholds rung is folded into metric, and the strict rung is dropped as well unless a continuous indicator is left to carry a residual variance; when only some declared items are dichotomous, both rungs are kept and a message names those items, whose thresholds and residual variances the rungs leave untested.

estimator

Estimator passed to lavaan. Defaults to "ML"; use "MLR" for robust corrections, in which case the likelihood ratio tests use the scaled difference. When ordered is supplied, a maximum likelihood or generalized least squares (the "GLS" label; Browne, 1974) estimator is replaced by "WLSMV", and "DWLS" and "ULS" are replaced by "WLSMV" and "ULSMV". That second substitution changes only the test: in lavaan "WLSMV" is "DWLS" and "ULSMV" is "ULS" with the mean and variance adjusted statistic, which is what makes the rung-to-rung difference test asymptotically valid for ordered data. The one categorical estimator left alone is "WLS", the full weight matrix estimator of Browne (1984) and Muthén (1984), whose statistic is asymptotically chi square already and whose weight matrix a substitution would silently change.

missing

Missing data handling passed to lavaan: one of "fiml" (the default) or "ml" (full information maximum likelihood, which fits every case with an observed item), "listwise" (listwise deletion), "pairwise", "two_stage", or "robust_two_stage" (two-stage maximum likelihood, with normal theory or nonnormality robust standard errors and tests; lavaan's "two.stage" and "robust.two.stage" are accepted for these two). Full information maximum likelihood and two-stage estimation are not available with the categorical estimator, and two-stage estimation needs estimator = "ML"; asking for another combination is an error. The default analysis is full information maximum likelihood whenever a value of a model variable is missing and the complete data analysis otherwise, unlike fa_confirmatory, which fits complete data by FIML too: data in which no such value is missing, or none but in cases with every model variable missing (which both treatments set aside), are fitted as they stand (under FIML the robust indices of an MLR ladder would be the corrected ones of Zhang and Savalei, 2023, not the complete data ones), and incomplete data by FIML. FIML needs continuous items, estimator = "ML" or "MLR", standard errors other than se = "robust.sem", and a test other than the Satorra-Bentler kind passed through ...; when the default meets incomplete items and one of these, the call stops and names the option to choose (missing = "listwise", "pairwise" for ordered items, estimator = "MLR", or, with estimator = "MLR", leaving out test) rather than deleting cases unasked, and an explicit missing = "fiml" with se = "robust.sem" or such a test stops too, whether or not a value is missing, since lavaan would fit the complete cases instead. Under FIML a group that never observes a variable of the model, or never observes two of them together, is refused before any fit (an error of class dmar_group_coverage). See Details.

group_partial

Character vector of parameters to leave free across groups at every rung, passed to lavaan's group.partial. Either user-supplied parameter labels or lavaan parameter specifications such as "visual =~ x2" or "x2 ~1". This is the partial invariance case of Byrne, Shavelson, and Muthén (1989). NULL (default) constrains everything the rung calls for, as does an empty vector (character(0) or lavaan's own default ""), which frees nothing in lavaan either.

parameterization

Identification of ordered indicators, passed to lavaan: "delta" (the default, lavaan's) or "theta". Residual variances are free parameters only under "theta", so a strict rung requested with ordered items switches to "theta" with a message. Ignored when no item is ordered.

...

Further arguments passed to cfa at every rung (for example std.lv, orthogonal, cluster). lavaan's own group.partial is merged into group_partial, and an empty one (NULL, character(0), or "") frees nothing, as in lavaan, so a call such as group.partial = if (free) terms else NULL runs either way; group.equal, which the ladder sets rung by rung, is an error here (choose the rungs with levels).

Value

A tidy wide data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with one row per fitted level and columns level (label), chi_square, df, p_chi_square (exact-fit test), cfi, rmsea, and, from the second row on, the step-comparison columns delta_chi_square, delta_df, p_value (the likelihood ratio test against the previous rung), delta_cfi, and delta_rmsea. delta_chi_square and p_value are NA wherever delta_df is zero, since a difference test on zero degrees of freedom tests nothing. Attributes carry the non-numeric information: "fits", the named list of fitted lavaan objects, one per level; "estimator", the estimator actually used; "ordered", TRUE when any indicator was declared ordered; "test", naming the chi square difference test used (NA when a single rung was fit and nothing was compared, and for a ULS ladder of continuous items without a corrected statistic, which has no difference test); "fit_indices", the version of the cfi and rmsea columns at every rung, "standard", "robust", or "scaled" ("robust" is the corrected indices of Zhang and Savalei, 2023, under FIML and two-stage estimation, and "scaled" the fallback of a ladder of ordered items, or fit by FIML or in two stages, with a scaled statistic whose robust indices lavaan did not compute at every rung); "fit_columns", the lines printed under the table that name that version for a ladder fit by FIML, one that fell back from the robust indices, or one whose robust indices DMAR computed, and that say why columns of a ULS ladder of continuous items are NA, or why the rmsea of a rung with zero degrees of freedom that does not fit exactly is (NULL otherwise; a two-stage ladder names the version in its own lines); "model_test", naming the statistic in the chi_square column at every rung ("standard", "scaled", or under the two-stage options the two-stage residual based or scaled statistic); for a two-stage ladder, "two_stage", a list with the method, the lines printed under the table, and, in rows, the cases the first stage read in each group and lavaan's count of them when an auxiliary variable was named, how many were observed on an auxiliary variable alone, whether the rungs were computed again with all of them (corrected), and whether the estimates of a rung that constrains across groups were too (reestimated); and "model", the lavaan syntax that was fitted.

Details

The models are nested by construction, each adding equality constraints across groups to the previous. With continuous indicators the constraint sets are none (beyond the configuration), then group.equal = "loadings", then c("loadings", "intercepts"), then c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals").

The ordered ladder differs, and the difference is substantive rather than cosmetic. For an ordered indicator the observed response is a coarsening of an underlying continuous response at a set of thresholds, and it is the thresholds, not an intercept, that locate the item on the latent scale. Constraining loadings while leaving thresholds free across groups therefore does not deliver what metric invariance is supposed to deliver, and the accepted sequence (Millsap & Yun-Tein, 2004; Wu & Estabrook, 2016) constrains thresholds first: "thresholds", then c("thresholds", "loadings") for metric, then c("thresholds", "loadings", "intercepts") for scalar, then adding "residuals" for strict. The intercept rung is not vacuous even when every indicator is ordered: once thresholds and loadings are constrained, lavaan frees the underlying-response intercepts in the non-reference groups, and the scalar rung is what returns them to zero and lets the latent means be estimated instead. Residual variances, however, are free parameters only under the theta parameterization, so parameterization switches to "theta" when a strict rung is requested with ordered items.

Dichotomous items are the exception the ordered ladder has to make room for. A two-category item contributes one threshold, and that threshold, the intercept of the underlying response, and its residual variance are not separately identified: the data give one proportion per group per item, which pins down a single standardized location and nothing else (Millsap & Yun-Tein, 2004; Wu & Estabrook, 2016). Constraining thresholds alone across groups is then a reparameterization rather than a restriction, since lavaan frees the underlying-response intercepts by exactly as many parameters as the constraint removes, and the residual variances stay fixed at one in every group whichever parameterization is in force. So the function counts the observed categories of each declared ordered indicator before building the ladder, and a message explains what the count implies. When all of them are dichotomous the thresholds rung is folded into metric, which constrains thresholds and loadings together; the strict rung goes too when every indicator in the model was declared ordered, leaving configural, metric, scalar. A continuous indicator alongside dichotomous ones keeps the strict rung, since its residual variance is a free parameter. When only some declared items are dichotomous the full ordered ladder is kept, since the polytomous items still carry testable thresholds and residual variances, and the message names the dichotomous items so their contribution to those two rungs is not overread. Every rung that is dropped is one that would have cost zero degrees of freedom.

When the estimator carries a robust test, the difference between two chi square statistics is not itself chi square distributed. lavTestLRT then returns the scaled difference test (the Satorra-Bentler or Satorra correction, chosen by lavaan to match the test in force), and that is what delta_chi_square and p_value report; the "test" attribute names the test used. In that case the model-level chi_square, p_chi_square, cfi, and rmsea columns are lavaan's scaled and robust versions, so delta_chi_square will not equal the difference of consecutive chi_square entries. That is a property of scaled difference testing, not an inconsistency.

One version of the test and one of the indices hold every rung, so that delta_cfi and delta_rmsea compare like with like, and the "model_test" and "fit_indices" attributes name the versions the columns hold. Where lavaan does not compute the robust indices at every rung, every rung falls back to one other version, and a line under the table says which. For a maximum likelihood fit of continuous items, whose robust indices estimate the population values of the ML indices with their small sample bias corrected for nonnormality, it is the standard indices, which estimate the same population values with the bias corrected as if the data were normal; the scaled indices, which put the scaled statistic into the standard formulas, estimate population values that change with the kurtosis of the data (Savalei, 2018). Beside the older mean and variance adjusted statistic (test = "mean.var.adjusted", passed through ...) lavaan computes no robust indices, and they are computed here, as sem_fit_measures computes them: they do not depend on which corrected statistic accompanies them (Savalei, 2018), so they equal those of the Satorra-Bentler statistic of the same fit, and a line under the table says that DMAR computed them. For ordered items, whose standard statistic is not the basis of an index, it is the scaled indices: lavaan leaves the robust indices NA at the rungs that constrain the thresholds under the default delta parameterization, as in the ordered example below. A ladder of continuous items fit by ULS (estimator = "ULS", "ULSM", or "ULSMV") withholds the ML-derived robust RMSEA and incremental indices (Savalei, 2018). Invariance to a common change of units alone does not establish validity outside their derivation. Eligible scaled indices are reported with a qualification: they do not estimate the same population discrepancy as ML-based indices, and ML cutoffs do not automatically apply. The standard ULS statistic is in the units of squared covariances, so its CFI and RMSEA are withheld too. At a rung that restricts the means, as the scalar and strict rungs do through the intercepts, the ULS fit function adds the squared mean residuals, in the squared units of the items, to the squared covariance residuals, in the squared units of the covariances, so the statistic, the loadings, and every index change with the units: on the first example under "ULSM", the scalar CFI is .9885 for the raw scores and .9840 with every score divided by 10, and the scalar delta CFI -.00005 and -.0046, a judgment against the cutoff of Cheung and Rensvold (2002) that turns on the units. The cfi and rmsea columns of such a rung are NA, and the chi_square column and the difference test are kept, since their reference distribution does not depend on the units, though their values do. A ladder fit by estimator = "ULS" alone is tested by Browne's residual based statistic, which has no units, and its cfi and rmsea columns, formed from that statistic, are reported at the rungs whose ULS estimates do not change with the units, those that leave the means free. At a rung that restricts the means through parameters the covariances share, as the scalar and strict rungs do through the loadings, which enter the means through the latent means, the ULS estimates change with the units, and so do Browne's statistic evaluated at them and the indices formed from it: on the first example, the scalar CFI is .8874 for the raw scores and .8861 with every score divided by 10, and the scalar delta CFI -.0212 and -.0225. Those columns are NA there too, and the chi_square column is kept. lavaan's difference test of a ULS ladder without a corrected statistic refers the difference of the ULS statistics, in the units of the squared covariances and not chi square distributed, to the chi square distribution, so delta_chi_square and p_value are NA at every rung, and "test" is NA; "ULSM" and "ULSMV" give a scaled difference test. estimator = "MLR", which does not depend on the units, is the estimator for nonnormal continuous items. When lavaan reports no scaled statistic at every rung (beside a bootstrap test, test = "bollen.stine"), the chi_square column and the difference test are the standard ones, and the attributes say so. A saturated rung (zero degrees of freedom and a statistic of zero) fits exactly in every version and does not decide, since lavaan can leave its robust CFI NA there from a ratio of zeros, or not compute it. Its statistic is zero in every version, and with it the model term of the CFI, \(T - c \cdot df\), whatever the scaling constant \(c\) (which is 0/0 there), so its cfi is 1 in every version; its RMSEA, \(\sqrt{(T - c \cdot df)/(N \cdot df)}\), is 0/0, which no version defines, and it keeps lavaan's 0, the convention lavaan applies in every version to a model that fits exactly, so that delta_cfi and delta_rmsea at the next rung compare with exact fit. A rung with zero degrees of freedom whose statistic is not zero, as when an inequality bound binds (lavaan's count of the degrees of freedom leaves the bound out), does not fit exactly: its cfi is formed from its statistic and decides the version of the indices (a ladder whose robust CFI lavaan leaves NA at such a rung falls back to another version at every rung, the standard indices for a maximum likelihood ladder of continuous items), while its rmsea, which divides by the degrees of freedom, is undefined and NA, as is delta_rmsea at the next rung, with a line under the table that says so; it does not decide the version of the test, which no version defines on zero degrees of freedom.

Which estimators carry such a test is worth being precise about, because a naive chi square difference on ordered data is not asymptotically valid. "MLM", "MLMV", "MLR", "WLSM", "WLSMV", "ULSM", and "ULSMV" carry one. "DWLS" and "ULS" do not, which is why declaring ordered items promotes them to "WLSMV" and "ULSMV": the discrepancy function and hence the parameter estimates are untouched, and only the statistic changes. The remaining case is "WLS", the full weight matrix estimator, whose statistic is asymptotically chi square under the theory of Browne (1984) and Muthén (1984) and so needs no correction; the "test" attribute reports the standard difference test there. The sample size that theory asks for is large, which limits full weighted least squares to large samples, but that is a separate matter from whether the difference test is the right one.

Full information maximum likelihood. With missing = "fiml" (the default when an item value is missing) or "ml", so that the ladder uses every case with an observed item, as fa_confirmatory fits the same model by default, the chi_square column is the FIML likelihood ratio statistic (its scaled version with estimator = "MLR"), and the cfi and rmsea columns are lavaan's robust versions, the corrected indices of Zhang and Savalei (2023) that fa_confirmatory reports for the same model: the complete data fit function evaluated at the FIML estimates, with the saturated FIML estimates in place of the sample moments, so that they estimate the values the indices would have had with complete data (lavaan uses their version 6, which assumes normality, and their version 3, which does not, with estimator = "MLR"). The usual indices computed from the FIML statistic move with the amount and kind of missing data (Zhang & Savalei, 2023), so their change from rung to rung is not the change complete data would show, and a cutoff for a change in fit, such as the delta CFI of about -.01 of Cheung and Rensvold (2002), is a statement about the latter. delta_cfi and delta_rmsea therefore compare the corrected indices, and one version holds every rung: when lavaan cannot compute them at some rung with degrees of freedom, every rung reports its scaled indices (for a fit with a scaled statistic) or its standard ones, and the line under the table says which. lavaan cannot combine FIML with the Satorra-Bentler or the mean and variance adjusted statistic (test = "satorra.bentler" or "mean.var.adjusted" passed through ...), nor with se = "robust.sem": it fits the complete cases instead, with a warning. Under the default of missing such a ladder is fitted as it stands when no item value is missing and stops otherwise; asked for by name, FIML with one of them stops before any fit whether or not a value is missing, as in fa_confirmatory, and so does a ladder whose fits lavaan made by another treatment than the FIML asked for (it fits estimator = "GLS", "WLS", and "ULS" in two stages).

FIML estimates the means, variances, and covariances of the model's variables within each group, so every group must observe every variable, and every pair of them together, at least once. A group that does not is refused by name before any fit, in an error of class dmar_group_coverage that carries the variables and pairs at issue (see dmar_metadata); lavaan would stop with an internal error. holzinger_swineford is such a data set, by school: t25_paper_form_board_r and t26_flags were given in Grant-White only. The message names what to do: leave the variable (or one of the pair) out of the model, or an auxiliary variable out of aux, for this comparison, so that the ladder compares the groups on what every group observes, or, when at least two groups would remain, leave the groups at issue out of data. Listwise deletion is no remedy, since a group that never observes a variable, or never observes two together, has no case observed on every variable, and the listwise ladder would stop on that group instead.

Auxiliary variables passed through ... as lavaan's aux enter a FIML fit as saturated correlates (Graham, 2003), and lavaan makes the mean and variance of each one ordinary parameters of each group, which the intercepts and residuals rungs would equate across the groups; the rung tests would then test whether the auxiliary is distributed alike in the groups, which says nothing about the measurement model. They are left free at every rung, beside any group_partial terms, so the ladder has the degrees of freedom of the ladder without the auxiliary. On six Holzinger and Swineford tests by school with 60 sentence completion scores deleted at random and general information (whose means are 44.8 and 36.6 in the two schools) as the auxiliary, the scalar rung's difference test is 23.88 on 4 df and its delta CFI -.031 (24.03 and -.031 without the auxiliary).

Two-stage estimation. With missing = "two_stage" every rung is fit in two stages (Yuan & Bentler, 2000; Savalei & Bentler, 2009): the means and covariances are first estimated in each group by maximum likelihood under the saturated normal model (the EM estimates, which use every partially observed case and any auxiliary variables passed through ... as lavaan's aux), and the rung is then fit to them by the complete data maximum likelihood discrepancy function. A case observed on an auxiliary variable but on none of the model's variables is read by the first stage and kept, as in fa_confirmatory, which says why: lavaan's two-stage estimator leaves such a case out of its sample size, so every rung is computed again with its sample size in each group set to the cases the first stage read there. The statistics, the indices, the difference tests, and the fits of the "fits" attribute then count every case. The second stage weights each group's discrepancy by its share of the sample size, so a rung that constrains parameters across groups has estimates that depend on the groups' counts, and when those grow in different ratios the rung is estimated again; the configural rung, which constrains nothing across groups, keeps lavaan's estimates. On six Holzinger and Swineford tests by school with the whole block missing for 77 pupils at random given general information (the auxiliary), 130 and 94 cases with an observed test grow to 156 and 145 read; the common intercept of lozenges at the scalar rung is 18.00 (SE .697) rather than lavaan's 18.21 (SE .782), and the scalar rung's difference test is 14.97 on 4 df, against 10.86 from lavaan's own ladder, 16.46 under FIML with the same auxiliary, and 17.44 after listwise deletion. A message says how many such cases there are, and a line under the table names the sample size. lavaan's summary() of a fit in the "fits" attribute counts them as used, and lavTestLRT warns that a difference test between such a fit and one lavaan made of the same data on its own sample size is invalid. The standard errors are the two-stage sandwich, and the chi_square column of each rung is the residual based statistic of Savalei and Bentler (2009, Eq. 8), whose rejection rate their simulations with incomplete normal data found close to the nominal level, and the statistic fa_confirmatory reports after two-stage estimation. With missing = "robust_two_stage" the standard errors are robust to nonnormality (Yuan & Bentler, 2000) and chi_square is lavaan's scaled statistic (Savalei & Falk, 2014). Under both, cfi and rmsea are lavaan's robust indices, the corrected indices of Zhang and Savalei (2023): their TS V2 after robust two-stage estimation, and its normal theory analog after normal theory two-stage estimation (fa_confirmatory explains the difference), so delta_cfi and delta_rmsea compare those, and the rung-to-rung test is the scaled difference test of Satorra and Bentler (2001), which lavTestLRT applies to two-stage fits. The difference is formed from the two rungs' naive statistics and their scaling, so delta_chi_square is not the difference of the chi_square entries. Two-stage estimation needs continuous items and estimator = "ML"; robustness to nonnormality comes from "robust_two_stage", not from estimator = "MLR". The residual based statistic treats every observed variable as random, so a model given as syntax that regresses on an observed variable needs fixed.x = FALSE passed through ...: under "two_stage" the statistic is refused for a fit that conditions on such a variable, as it is for sampling weights, clustered cases, inequality constraints, and a parameter on a bound, each with a message that says what to do instead.

A rung whose constraints cost no degrees of freedom tests nothing, so delta_chi_square and p_value are NA when delta_df is zero rather than reporting a difference in chi square that is numerical noise and can come out negative. The situation is reported in a message. It arises with dichotomous items (the ladder above avoids the two rungs where it is structural) and, for instance, with group_partial specifications that free every parameter a rung would constrain.

Failure at a rung does not end the conversation: partial invariance (freeing the offending parameter) is the usual next step, for which group_partial refits the whole ladder with named parameters free, and the "fits" attribute gives the fitted objects to lavTestScore for a score test of which constraint is doing the damage. This function deliberately reports the standard ladder rather than automating modification searches.

A rung whose likelihood has no maximum, flat or still rising as an error variance in some group falls below zero, has no estimates to compare, only the point where lavaan's optimizer stopped; the function checks each rung with a negative error variance as fa_bifactor describes and stops with an error of class dmar_no_maximum that names the rung, the group, and the item and prints the lavaan code of that rung's fit, where bounds = "pos.var" (also accepted through ... here) or a different model are the choices. Three items whose correlations in one group have a negative product give such a rung when std.lv = TRUE is passed through ...; under the default scaling by a marker item, lavaan's optimizer does not converge on such data. A negative error variance at a maximum of the likelihood is a finite estimate, and its rung is reported.

A rung that lavaan's optimizer does not converge on has no estimates to report, and the function stops with an error of class dmar_not_converged, the class fa_confirmatory gives such a fit, whose message names the rung. The condition carries the rung as level and the lavaan code that reproduces its fit as syntax (the model) and lavaan_call (the call, with my_data in place of the data).

Savalei, V., & Bentler, P. M. (2009). A two-stage approach to missing data: Theory and application to auxiliary variables. Structural Equation Modeling, 16, 477–497. doi:10.1080/10705510903008238

Savalei, V., & Falk, C. F. (2014). Robust two-stage approach outperforms robust full information maximum likelihood with incomplete nonnormal data. Structural Equation Modeling, 21(2), 280–302. doi:10.1080/10705511.2014.882692

Wu, H., & Estabrook, R. (2016). Identification of confirmatory factor analysis models of different levels of invariance for ordered categorical outcomes. Psychometrika, 81(4), 1014–1045. doi:10.1007/s11336-016-9506-0

Yuan, K.-H., & Bentler, P. M. (2000). Three likelihood-based methods for mean and covariance structure analysis with nonnormal missing data. Sociological Methodology, 30, 165–200.

Zhang, X., & Savalei, V. (2023). New computations for RMSEA and CFI following FIML and TS estimation with missing data. Psychological Methods, 28(2), 263–283. doi:10.1037/met0000445

See also

cfa_1 and fa_confirmatory for the single-group measurement models; reliability_omega for the reliability of the composite the model justifies; compare_cov_structures for covariance-structure comparisons outside the factor model; lavTestScore for the score test that localizes a failed rung.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Do the two schools measure the verbal and the reasoning construct
# in the same way? (Holzinger & Swineford, bundled.) The measurement
# model is a named list of factors; for a single factor, name its
# indicators with items = instead, or give lavaan syntax, as the last
# example does.
data(holzinger_swineford)
hs_factors <- list(
  verbal    = c("t6_paragraph_comprehension", "t7_sentence",
                "t9_word_meaning"),
  deduction = c("t20_deduction", "t22_problem_reasoning",
                "t23_series_completion"))

# The whole ladder, configural through metric, scalar, and strict.
# Configural invariance asks whether the same pattern of loadings
# holds at both schools; metric adds the constraint that the loadings
# are equal across schools, and it is the rung that has to hold before
# a relation involving one of these factors is compared across them;
# scalar equates the intercepts as well, which comparing factor means
# requires; strict equates the residual variances. Each row from the
# second on tests its rung against the one below it.
mi <- measurement_invariance(holzinger_swineford, hs_factors,
                             group = "school")
mi
#>  level      chi_square df p_chi_square cfi   rmsea delta_chi_square delta_df
#>  configural 22.505     16 0.1276       0.992 0.052 <NA>             <NA>    
#>  metric     36.346     20 0.0140       0.979 0.074 13.841           4       
#>  scalar     44.217     24 0.0072       0.974 0.075 7.871            4       
#>  strict     54.343     30 0.0042       0.969 0.073 10.126           6       
#>  p_value delta_cfi delta_rmsea
#>  <NA>    <NA>      <NA>       
#>  0.0078  -0.013    0.022      
#>  0.0964  -0.005    0.001      
#>  0.1195  -0.005    -0.001     

# The fitted models travel with the table, so localizing a failed rung
# costs no refitting.
names(attr(mi, "fits"))
#> [1] "configural" "metric"     "scalar"     "strict"    

# The broom verbs: one row per rung of the ladder, and the model-level
# summary (estimator, test flavor, fit index flavor).
generics::tidy(mi)
#>         term chi_square df p_chi_square       cfi      rmsea delta_chi_square
#> 1 configural   22.50471 16  0.127629786 0.9915883 0.05197395               NA
#> 2     metric   36.34593 20  0.014001841 0.9788619 0.07369221        13.841221
#> 3     scalar   44.21741 24  0.007197934 0.9738554 0.07481503         7.871474
#> 4     strict   54.34304 30  0.004209093 0.9685202 0.07342746        10.125635
#>   delta_df    p_value    delta_cfi  delta_rmsea
#> 1       NA         NA           NA           NA
#> 2        4 0.00781944 -0.012726402  0.021718262
#> 3        4 0.09640134 -0.005006486  0.001122817
#> 4        6 0.11945997 -0.005335160 -0.001387562
generics::glance(mi)
#>   n_levels estimator ordered                                test fit_indices
#> 1        4        ML   FALSE standard chi square difference test    standard

# Partial invariance frees one loading across the schools at every
# rung (Byrne, Shavelson, & Muthén, 1989), so the metric rung costs
# one degree of freedom fewer than it did above. Naming a leading
# subset of the rungs in levels = stops the ladder there, which keeps
# this and the next two examples quick; a reported analysis climbs
# the whole ladder.
measurement_invariance(holzinger_swineford, hs_factors,
                       group = "school",
                       group_partial = "verbal =~ t7_sentence",
                       levels = c("configural", "metric"))
#>  level      chi_square df p_chi_square cfi   rmsea delta_chi_square delta_df
#>  configural 22.505     16 0.1276       0.992 0.052 <NA>             <NA>    
#>  metric     30.789     19 0.0426       0.985 0.064 8.284            3       
#>  p_value delta_cfi delta_rmsea
#>  <NA>    <NA>      <NA>       
#>  0.0405  -0.007    0.012      

# With the indicators coded as ordered categories, ordered = TRUE puts
# the thresholds rung first, because thresholds rather than intercepts
# carry the location information there, and makes the rung-to-rung
# tests the scaled difference tests; the "test" attribute names the
# test that was used. The ladder stops at the thresholds rung here;
# metric, scalar, and strict follow it. lavaan computes no robust fit
# indices for the thresholds rung, so both rows report the scaled ones,
# as the line under the table says.
hs_ordered <- holzinger_swineford
for (item in unlist(hs_factors, use.names = FALSE)) {
  hs_ordered[[item]] <- as.integer(cut(
    holzinger_swineford[[item]],
    breaks = quantile(holzinger_swineford[[item]],
                      c(0, .25, .5, .75, 1)),
    include.lowest = TRUE))
}
mi_ordered <- measurement_invariance(hs_ordered, hs_factors,
                                     group = "school", ordered = TRUE,
                                     levels = c("configural",
                                                "thresholds"))
#> Ordered items declared: switching to estimator = "WLSMV".
mi_ordered
#>  level      chi_square df p_chi_square cfi   rmsea delta_chi_square delta_df
#>  configural 18.012     16 0.3232       0.999 0.029 <NA>             <NA>    
#>  thresholds 27.181     22 0.2044       0.996 0.040 10.330           6       
#>  p_value delta_cfi delta_rmsea
#>  <NA>    <NA>      <NA>       
#>  0.1114  -0.002    0.011      
#> 
#> cfi, rmsea: lavaan did not compute its robust versions at every rung, so these columns hold its scaled versions, which put the scaled statistic into the standard formulas; delta_cfi and delta_rmsea compare them
attr(mi_ordered, "test")
#> [1] "scaled chi square difference test (method = \"satorra.2000\")"

# The measurement model can also be given as lavaan syntax, and
# missing = "fiml", the default, fits the ladder by full information
# maximum likelihood when continuous items have incomplete cases; here
# twenty scores on one item are set to missing first. Naming it states
# the choice in the call. With three indicators
# the single factor is just identified in each group, so the
# configural row is saturated (zero degrees of freedom, exact fit)
# and the metric row carries the test. Under FIML the cfi and rmsea
# columns are the corrected indices of Zhang and Savalei (2023), as the
# line under the table says.
hs_missing <- holzinger_swineford
set.seed(113)
hs_missing$t7_sentence[sample(nrow(hs_missing), 20)] <- NA
measurement_invariance(
  hs_missing,
  model = "verbal =~ t6_paragraph_comprehension + t7_sentence +
           t9_word_meaning",
  group = "school", missing = "fiml",
  levels = c("configural", "metric"))
#>  level      chi_square df p_chi_square cfi   rmsea delta_chi_square delta_df
#>  configural 0.000      0  <NA>         1.000 0.000 <NA>             <NA>    
#>  metric     7.671      2  0.0216       0.987 0.140 7.671            2       
#>  p_value delta_cfi delta_rmsea
#>  <NA>    <NA>      <NA>       
#>  0.0216  -0.013    0.140      
#> 
#> cfi, rmsea: the FIML corrected indices of Zhang and Savalei (2023), version 6 (normal theory), which approximate the values complete data would give and are not computed from the chi_square column; delta_cfi and delta_rmsea compare them
